details: CONFIRMED by reading and by a probe: parse() of a new-shape item yields state/found/taken_by/closed_by/test, so changed(item, ip=5) picks exactly the old FIELD_ORDER keys and serialize() accepts the result; only _refuse_new_shape stands between a writer and the loss of found_at/taken_at/closed_at. The behaviour is correct today; the test would pass with it disabled, so a later edit of _item_at or done() (step 2 rewrites exactly these functions) can drop it unseen. LOW: correct today, fragile, cheap.

details: CONFIRMED by a probe. The brief names only found_at <= taken_at <= closed_at, so this is an edge it left out rather than a broken rule; the order list in check_new (`stamps = [found, taken, closed]`) simply omits dropped_at. Reachable only by a hand-edited or migrated file (step 2's migration invents times for old items, which is where a wrong dropped_at could appear). LOW: one more element in the order check.
evidence: python3 probe: p("done", dropped_at="2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", dropped_why=["no"]) with found_at 2026-10-23T21:16:10Z
failing_case: A done/ file with found_at "2026-10-23T21:16:10Z", dropped_at "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", dropped_why ["no"], taken_at/closed_at null: parse(..., "done") gives state "dropped" with no problem. It should be refused like closed_at before taken_at ("the times are not in order").
fix_hint: In check_new, also require found_at <= dropped_at when both parse (e.g. a second ordered list [found, dropped]), with a TestNewShape case.
pass_cases: 1. found_at 2026-10-23T21:16:10Z, dropped_at 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z (done/): a problem naming the order.
2. found_at 2026-10-23T21:16:10Z, dropped_at 2026-10-23T21:16:10Z (same second, done/): accepted, state dropped.
3. found_at 2026-10-23T21:16:10Z, dropped_at 2026-10-24T01:00:00Z (done/): accepted, state dropped (the DROPPED case of TestNewShape keeps passing).
findings.summary: a new-shape item dropped before it was found (dropped_at < found_at) passes the check

notes: Fine as built: every brief rule is present and tested (taken_by iff taken_at; found_at <= taken_at <= closed_at; closed_at needs taken_at and a test and the reverse; dropped_at iff dropped_why, excluding taken_at/closed_at; timestamps parse with strptime; folder rule via `where`; mixed keys refused; old shape untouched and not judged by folder). parse() gives one form (state, found, taken_by/test as "", closed_by) so no reader branches on shape; all readers pass the folder (Reader.items "open", closed_items "done", done() "open", merge hook "done"). merge.test.sh T15n3 would fail on master (unknown key found_at), so it does test the change. The writers that edit an existing item (set_ip, drop, release, take through _item_at; done directly) refuse a new-shape item; land replays raw text and add only reads ip/state.

Step-2 remarks: `relay queue json` now prints, for a new-shape item, both the events and the computed state/found/closed_by, with null taken_by/test shown as "" (the brief leaves widening json to step 2). The step-1 merge hook judges only done/ files the range ADDS, so step 2's migration of existing done/ files is not judged by it; that is consistent with today but means migrated files are checked only by readers marking them malformed.
Taste: no repeated waste added (three extra merges in merge.test.sh, seconds).
